raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary
- Add FP8 training for ZAYA1-8B (`fp8: hybrid`). CCA Q/K/V/O projections and expert SwiGLU GEMMs run as Transformer Engine linears (`parallel_mode="duplicated"`) under one FP8 autocast for the whole stack. The router, depthwise convolutions, RMSNorm, attention, embeddings, and the tied logits projection stay in BF16/FP32.
- Pad the token axis to a multiple of 8 before each TE GEMM. A top-1 route can hand one expert as few as 4 tokens, and TE FP8 needs the leading-dimension product divisible by 8. Reject FP8 GEMMs whose in or out features are not multiples of 16. The router stays BF16 because its last projection scores 17 classes.
- Add `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml` for MI300X and MI355X with `fp8_recipe: tensorwise`. Current scaling takes each scale from the tensor being cast, so FP8 is accurate from step 1 with no amax history. Delayed scaling starts with an empty history; on the released checkpoint a cold delayed-scaling forward scored SGLang rollouts at Pearson r 0.72.
- Switch the BF16 and FP8 ZAYA1 recipes to mock data so they run without a dataset mount. `vocab_size` stays 262272 from `zaya1.yaml`.
- Update `docs/04-technical-guides/zaya1/validation.md` and `docs/06-developer-guide/model-support-matrix.md`.

## Validation
Run on 1x MI300X node (tw042), `rocm/primus:v26.8`, TE 2.17.1, Megatron-LM `d3528a21`.

Log-prob parity against SGLang ([sgl-project/sglang#26347](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26347)): the same 4 GSM8K greedy rollouts used for BF16, 1,024 tokens each, scored by Primus with the `Zyphra/ZAYA1-base` weights and no FP8 warm-up.

| Rollout tokens (n=4096) | Pearson r | MAE | RMSE |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 0.978 | 0.010 | 0.055 |
| FP8 tensorwise, cold | 0.935 | 0.026 | 0.101 |
| FP8 delayed, cold | 0.720 | 0.155 | — |
| FP8 delayed, after 5 backward calibration passes | 0.893 | 0.033 | 0.142 |

GSM8K pretraining from scratch with the FP8 recipe (seq 128, global batch 8, lr 1e-5). Early losses track the BF16 validation run:

| Step | BF16 | FP8 tensorwise |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.820 | 12.873 |
| 10 | 11.229 | 10.911 |
| 30 | 7.597 | 7.791 |

No skipped or NaN iterations. The 30k-step run was not completed: at 3.2 s/step on 4 GPUs it needs about 27 h, beyond the 8 h job limit.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/unit_tests/megatron/transformer/zaya1` (20 passed on MI300X, including `test_cold_tensorwise_fp8_matches_high_precision`)
- [x] `pytest tests/trainer/test_megatron_trainer.py -k zaya1` (BF16 and FP8, 4 stages, 3 iterations, mock data)
- [x] `pre-commit run` on the changed files
- [ ] MI355X run of `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml` (not yet exercised on gfx950)
- [ ] Full 30k-step FP8 GSM8K run

## Module is imported with 'import' and 'import from' Module 'primus.backends.megatron.core.models.zaya1.zaya1_modules' is imported with both 'import' and 'import from'. --- Use one import style for this module throughout the file. Since this test needs the module object for monkeypatching, the cleanest fix is:

  • Keep the existing top-level from ... import (...) unchanged for current symbol usage.
  • Replace the inner import ... as zaya_modules with a module-object lookup via sys.modules[...], which avoids introducing a second import statement style while preserving behavior.

Concretely in tests/unit_tests/megatron/transformer/zaya1/test_zaya1_math.py:

  • Add import sys near the top-level imports.
  • In test_fp8_uses_te_linears_for_cca_and_experts_only, replace the inner import primus... as zaya_modules line with: 
    zaya_modules = sys.modules["primus.backends.megatron.core.models.zaya1.zaya1_modules"]

    • This keeps functionality intact and resolves the CodeQL finding.

 # ZAYA1-8B validation
 
-The checked-in recipes are `examples/megatron/configs/MI300X/zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` and `examples/megatron/configs/MI355X/zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml`. Those two files are the same recipe. The run below used that recipe with `train_iters: 30000` on GSM8K.
+The checked-in BF16 recipes are `zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` under `examples/megatron/configs/MI300X`, `MI325X`, and `MI355X`. They train on mock data (`mock_data: true`), so they need no dataset mount. They differ only in batch size: the MI300X and MI325X recipes fill GPU memory (see [Throughput](#throughput)), and MI355X reuses the MI300X batch sizes without having been run on MI355X. The run below used micro-batch 1 and global batch 8 with `train_iters: 30000` on GSM8K instead of mock data.
+
+The FP8 recipes are `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml` in the same three directories, also on mock data. They set `fp8: hybrid` with `fp8_recipe: tensorwise`. CCA Q/K/V/O projections and expert SwiGLU GEMMs are Transformer Engine FP8 linears. The router, depthwise convolutions, RMSNorm, attention, embeddings, and the tied logits projection stay in BF16. The training and parity numbers in this note are from the BF16 run.
+
+Tensorwise (current) scaling takes each FP8 scale from the tensor being cast, so FP8 is accurate from the first step of a cold start. Delayed scaling starts with an empty amax history. On the released checkpoint, a cold delayed-scaling forward scored SGLang's greedy GSM8K rollouts at Pearson r 0.72 (BF16 gives 0.98) and stayed there until training-style backward passes filled the amax history. Keep `fp8_recipe: delayed` only for runs that warm the history before the steps that matter.

-That comparison checks the loaded checkpoint forward (CCA, router, residual scaling, RMSNorm). It is not a second training run. The unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/megatron/transformer/zaya1/` lock the same formulas on a tiny config: residual affine `(x + bias) * scale`, raw key temperature, vector EDA, mixture-of-depths skip, RMSNorm, builder wiring, and one forward/backward.
+That comparison checks the loaded checkpoint forward (CCA, router, residual scaling, RMSNorm). It is not a second training run. The unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/megatron/transformer/zaya1/` lock the same formulas on a tiny config: residual affine `(x + bias) * scale`, raw key temperature, vector EDA, mixture-of-depths skip, RMSNorm, builder wiring, one forward/backward, and a cold tensorwise FP8 forward checked against the same weights in high precision.
+
+## Throughput
+
+The MI300X and MI325X recipes were run as checked in on one 8-GPU node with `rocm/primus:v26.8` (PyTorch 2.14.0, Transformer Engine 2.17.1): 30 steps of mock data, sequence length 128, data parallel 8, one micro-batch per GPU per step. Each micro-batch size is the largest multiple of 8 that completes the recipe, including the end-of-training evaluation. Step time is the median, tokens/s/GPU the harmonic mean, and TFLOP/s/GPU the mean over steps 6 to 30.
+
+| GPU | Precision | Micro / global batch | Step time | Tokens/s/GPU | TFLOP/s/GPU | Peak memory per GPU | Next size up |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| MI300X | BF16 | 128 / 1024 | 1635 ms | 10016 | 118.6 | 181 of 192 GB | 136 stalls in evaluation |
+| MI300X | FP8 | 120 / 960 | 1814 ms | 8478 | 100.4 | 187 of 192 GB | 128 runs out of memory |
+| MI325X | BF16 | 216 / 1728 | 2049 ms | 13426 | 159.0 | 249 of 256 GB | 224 runs out of memory |
+| MI325X | FP8 | 184 / 1472 | 2118 ms | 11154 | 132.1 | 245 of 256 GB | 192 runs out of memory |
+
+TFLOP/s/GPU is Megatron's analytic GPT estimate with ZAYA1's dimensions. It models neither CCA nor the alternation of attention and MoE stages, so compare it only between ZAYA1 runs.
+
+Memory per GPU is a fixed 74 GB (BF16) or 87 GB (FP8) for weights, gradients, sharded optimizer state, and runtime buffers, plus about 0.8 GB per sample, mostly fp32 logits over the 262k vocabulary. FP8 holds extra FP8 weight copies, so it fits fewer samples. It is also slower than BF16 here: with hidden size 2048 and top-1 routing over 16 experts, the expert GEMMs are small, and the FP8 casts cost more than the faster GEMMs save.
+
+The FP8 recipes set `NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON: "0"` in their `env:` block. The runner turns on Transformer Engine's Triton cast-transpose by default, and that kernel autotunes for each new tensor shape. Expert token counts change every step, so with the Triton kernel the MI325X FP8 run at micro-batch 64 spent 307 s on its first step and still took 2 to 10 s per step at steps 11 to 15, against 1.8 s with the HIP cast kernel.

+work_group: ${PRIMUS_TEAM:amd}
+user_name: ${PRIMUS_USER:root}
+exp_name: ${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME:zaya1-fp8-pretrain}
+workspace: ${PRIMUS_WORKSPACE:./output}
+
+# The runner enables Transformer Engine's Triton FP8 cast-transpose, which
+# autotunes once per new tensor shape. Expert token counts change every step,
+# so it keeps retuning and FP8 steps stall. The HIP cast kernel has no
+# per-shape cost.
+env:
+  NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON: "0"
+
+modules:
+  pre_trainer:
+    framework: megatron
+    config: pre_trainer.yaml
+
+    # Full ZAYA1-base shape lives in zaya1.yaml (80 stages, hidden 2048).
+    model: zaya1.yaml
+    overrides:
+      wandb_project: "Primus_Pretrain"
+      stderr_sink_level: DEBUG
+
+      log_avg_skip_iterations: 1
+      log_avg_reset_interval: 10
+
+      # 30-step mock-data run for one 8-GPU node (DP=8). FP8 keeps BF16 master
+      # weights and adds cached FP8 weight copies, so it fits fewer samples
+      # than BF16. micro_batch_size 120 is the largest multiple of 8 that
+      # completes on MI300X with rocm/primus:v26.8: it peaks at 187 of 192 GB
+      # per GPU, and 128 runs out of memory. On fewer GPUs, lower
+      # micro_batch_size or num_layers (keep it even). Do not edit the model
+      # yaml to shrink the architecture.
+      train_iters: 30
+      micro_batch_size: 120
+      # One micro batch per GPU per step at DP=8.
+      # Must be divisible by micro_batch_size * data_parallel_size.
+      global_batch_size: 960
+      seq_length: 128
+      max_position_embeddings: 4096
+
+      lr: 1.0e-5
+      min_lr: 0.0
+      lr_warmup_iters: 1
+      lr_decay_iters: null
+      lr_decay_style: cosine
+      weight_decay: 0.1
+      adam_beta1: 0.9
+      adam_beta2: 0.95
+      eod_mask_loss: true
+      init_method_std: 0.02
+
+      # Data parallel only. TP, PP, CP, EP and sequence parallel are rejected
+      # by zaya1_builder.
+      tensor_model_parallel_size: 1
+      pipeline_model_parallel_size: 1
+      context_parallel_size: 1
+      expert_model_parallel_size: 1
+      sequence_parallel: false
+      overlap_grad_reduce: false
+      overlap_param_gather: false
+      gradient_accumulation_fusion: false
+
+      # Synthetic tokens. The mock-data patch forces NullTokenizer and
+      # clears these paths; vocab_size stays 262272 from zaya1.yaml.
+      mock_data: true
+      train_data_path: null
+      valid_data_path: null
+      test_data_path: null
+      eval_interval: 100
+      eval_iters: 8
+
+      finetune: false
+      auto_continue_train: false
+      load: null
+      no_load_optim: null
+      no_load_rng: null
+      save: null
+      save_interval: 20000
+      no_save_optim: null
+      no_save_rng: null
+      disable_last_saving: true
+      ckpt_format: torch
+
+      enable_primus_turbo: false
+      use_turbo_attention: false
+      use_turbo_grouped_gemm: false
+
+      # Hybrid FP8: E4M3 forward, E5M2 backward. CCA Q/K/V/O and expert
+      # SwiGLU run as TE GEMMs. Router, conv, RMSNorm, attention, embeddings,
+      # and the tied logits projection stay in BF16.

+      fp8_recipe: tensorwise

+    # Every FP8 GEMM needs in and out features divisible by 16.
+    config = _tiny_config(
+        num_attention_heads=2,
+        kv_channels=16,
+        ffn_hidden_size=32,
+        moe_ffn_hidden_size=32,
+        zaya_mlp_expansion=16,
+        zaya_balance_lr=0.0,
+        fp8="hybrid",
+        fp8_recipe="tensorwise",
+    )
+    set_args(_args())
+    model = get_model_provider("zaya1")(pre_process=True, post_process=True, config=config)
+    cca = model.decoder.layers[0].self_attn
+    assert isinstance(cca.linear_q, _Fp8Linear)
+    assert isinstance(model.decoder.layers[1].zaya_block.local_experts[0].linear_fc1, _Fp8Linear)
+
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    model.to(device).eval()
+    batch, seq, vocab = 2, 16, 64
+    input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), device=device)
+    position_ids = torch.arange(seq, device=device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        fp8_logits = model(input_ids, position_ids, attention_mask=None).float()
+        config.fp8 = None
+        ref_logits = model(input_ids, position_ids, attention_mask=None).float()
+        config.fp8 = "hybrid"
+    assert torch.isfinite(fp8_logits).all()
+    cosine = F.cosine_similarity(fp8_logits.flatten(), ref_logits.flatten(), dim=0)
+    assert cosine > 0.99, f"cold FP8 logits drifted from high precision: cosine={cosine:.4f}"
+
+    model.train()
+    labels = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), device=device)
+    loss = model(input_ids, position_ids, attention_mask=None, labels=labels)
+    assert torch.isfinite(loss).all()
+    loss.sum().backward()
+    assert torch.isfinite(cca.linear_q.linear.weight.grad).all()
